watchlist_finding: The new canvas has NO dedicated watchlist screen under any current artboard id. Full-text search of every *.dc.html file in docs/design/redesign-2026-08/ for 'watchlist' returns exactly 2 hits, both identical: an IconButton icon="plus" label="watchlist" in the Asset Detail header (lines 540 and 611 of '03 Home and Markets.dc.html', screens s26 'Asset detail · About' and s27 'Asset detail · Order book') — i.e. an 'add to watchlist' toggle with no screen anywhere that lets the investor view the resulting list. Searches for 'saved', 'following', 'star', 'my list', and 'favor(ite)' across all canvas files return zero hits — the watchlist is not designed under any alternate name either. This is a broken/incomplete flow as designed: you can add a stock to your watchlist from the asset page, but there is no artboard showing 'my watchlist'. The app's own watchlist_screen.dart (lib/screens/markets/watchlist_screen.dart, lines 170-181) already documents half of this: its code comments say the PRE-CONSOLIDATION canvas ('grew 66 -> 97 screens', per price_alerts_screen.dart's header) had a Watchlist screen at old-id s46 whose footer note named it as one of only two entry points into a Price Alerts screen at old-id s86. That old s46 has been dropped entirely from the current 56-artboard canvas (current s46 is 'Sell step 2 - Your price per share' in '04 Buy and Sell.dc.html', an unrelated screen) and was never replaced with a new watchlist artboard. Price alerts ARE fully designed in the current canvas, but as a self-contained loop that does not depend on a watchlist screen: 'Set a price alert' (s49) is reached from the Asset Detail page itself (specifically its market-closed variant, s39, via a 'Set a price alert' button — the open-market asset page s26/s27 does not show this button anywhere), and s49 links to 'My alerts' (s50), a flat list of the investor's alerts (each with its own absolute rises-above/falls-below price threshold) with a 'New alert' button that loops back to s49. So: the canvas's price-alerts feature is complete and does not require a watchlist screen to function, but the app's actual watchlist_screen.dart is architecturally load-bearing in the live app — Routes.priceAlerts has exactly one call site in the whole codebase, watchlist_screen.dart's 'Manage price alerts' button — so deleting/redesigning Watchlist without adding a replacement entry point would strand the app's real, backend-CRUD-wired Price Alerts management screen (lib/screens/markets/price_alerts_screen.dart) with no way to reach it, even though the canvas's OWN price-alert flow doesn't need that entry point. Separately, the app's alert data model (percent-of-day-move presets '±3%/±5%/±10%' plus a per-watchlist-hub editor) does not match the canvas's model (one alert per asset, absolute ₦ price + direction, set from that asset's own page) at all -- see price_alerts_screen.dart's evidence entry below.
home_variants_finding: 'Home Variants.dc.html' is a standalone, orphaned exploration file: nothing in any other canvas file links to it (grepped 'Home Variants' and '#l1'/'#3e'/'nav.l1'/'nav.3e' across every *.dc.html — the only hits are the file's own internal self-links). Its own heading text (line 34) reads 'Kudimata Invest · home · 3E approved, light reworked' and the section title (line 35) is 'Home, final pair'. Artboard id="l1" is captioned 'Light · reworked' with a closing note 'Light card: paper + hairline, purple tint chips, illustration locked into the top row.' Artboard id="3e" is captioned 'Dark · approved' with closing note 'Approved: neutral charcoal, dark grey money card, purple accents, clean navbar.' Together they read as a two-artboard exercise to finalize ONE visual detail (the money-card surface treatment and a 4-action evenly-spaced quick-action row: Add/Withdraw/Invest/Learn, no Orders action) across light and dark, not a competing full Home design. The canonical, currently-wired Home is s22 ('22 · Home, verified') and s23 ('23 · Home, first time (verification not finished)') in '03 Home and Markets.dc.html', section 3 of 6 -- confirmed canonical because every other canvas file that refers to Home does so by that section/screen number ('01 Getting In.dc.html' line 677: 'Look around → Section 3 (Home)'; '02 Verification.dc.html' line 751: 'Browse → Section 3 (Markets)'), and s22/s23 are the versions all downstream screens (s24 Markets, s26/27 Asset detail, etc.) link back to via their own nav objects. Note s22/s23 themselves diverge from what l1/3e (and s22/23's own section-header prose) describe: the header text for section 3 promises 'four round actions' but s22/s23 actually render FIVE (Add/Withdraw/Invest/Orders/Learn) in a horizontal-scroll row, whereas l1/3e literally have four, evenly spaced, with no Orders action -- i.e. l1/3e is closer to the file's own written spec than s22/23 is. That inconsistency is itself worth flagging to the human, but does not change which pair is canonical: s22/s23 are.

screens.purpose: Home tab root. Two structurally different bodies: verified investor (balance/portfolio panel with inline wallet-balance row, 3 quick actions [Add money/Buy shares/Orders], AI 'week in the market' digest card, 'Your holdings' list, conditional Watchlist strip, conditional Trending list) vs not-verified investor (3-step 'Get set up' checklist panel, single 'Biggest mover today' row).
screens.evidence: Searched canvas for 'Total wealth' and 'Grow with Kudimata' (both found in s22/s22d, lines 59 and 76 of '03 Home and Markets.dc.html') and for 'Finish verifying to start investing' (found in s23/s23d, line 219) -- these are the canonical current Home artboards (see home_variants_finding for why s22/s23, not l1/3e, are canonical). The app's own code comments cite canvas ids 's29' (verified) and 's30' (not-verified) throughout (home_screen.dart lines 1-14, 395, 669) -- STALE: in the current canvas s29/s29d are 'Step 4 Review, naming your price' and s30/s30d are 'Step 6 PIN, then order placed', both in '04 Buy and Sell.dc.html', unrelated Buy-flow screens. Content diverges substantially from s22/s23 even after correcting for the renumbering: canvas s22 has NO digest card, NO 'Your holdings' list, NO watchlist strip, NO trending list -- instead it has a 'Grow with Kudimata' pair of education cards (readiness check + money-persona quiz) and a financial-literacy lesson row, none of which the app builds. Canvas s22's quick-action row has 5 actions in a horizontal scroll (Add/Withdraw/Invest/Orders/Learn); the app has 3 in a fixed row (Add money/Buy shares/Orders) -- Withdraw and Learn are absent as Home quick actions in the app.
screens.why: The app's holdings-list/watchlist-strip/trending-list/AI-digest sections are all real, live-data-backed features added in direct response to user reports (per the file's own extensive header comments) that have no equivalent anywhere in canvas s22/s23, which instead centers on education content (readiness quiz, persona quiz, literacy lessons) the app doesn't build at all. Redesigning to s22/s23 literally would delete working, user-requested features; restyling only would leave the education-content half of the canvas's Home unimplemented. A human must decide which content wins.

screens.purpose: Pushed search screen: back + search pill header, live local-filter results list (AssetRow), persisted 'Recent' search-history chips, a nudge card ('Not sure what to search for?'), footer ghost 'Browse all of the market' button.
screens.evidence: Searched for 'Search companies' (the placeholder text) and found it in both the app (search_screen.dart line 127) and the canvas at s24/s24d ('03 Home and Markets.dc.html' lines 391, 463) and s25/s25d (the actual Search screen, lines 1073-1129, card-titled '25 · Search'). s25's shell matches: back button + search pill, then an AssetRow results list, matching-result rows navigate to the asset. Differences: canvas s25 shows 'Popular this week' suggested-ticker chips (MTNN/GTCO/ZENITHBANK/AIRTELAFRI, a curated/trending set), not the app's personalized 'Recent' search-history chips; canvas s25 has no NudgeCard and no footer 'Browse all of the market' button. The mechanical shortlist for this screen (s24 Markets 0.31, s33 Portfolio 0.172, s55 Corporate actions 0.138) never surfaced s25 at all -- found only by reading the full canvas file. The app's own comment citing canvas '#s31' is STALE: current s31 = 'Order placed' (post-PIN confirmation, '04 Buy and Sell.dc.html'), not Search.
screens.why: Core shell (back+pill+results list navigating to asset detail) matches s25 closely enough for a direct redesign; the 'Recent' vs 'Popular this week' chip-source difference and the extra NudgeCard/footer button are additive, low-risk deviations a designer/engineer can reconcile without a ruling on deleting any live feature.

screens.evidence: Searched for 'watchlist' and found the exact plus-icon 'add to watchlist' affordance the app implements at s26/s27's header (IconButton icon="plus" label="watchlist", lines 540 and 611) -- matches the app's `icon: watched ? 'check' : 'plus'` toggle almost exactly. Searched for 'Buy'/'Sell' sticky footer and found the same two-button pattern at the bottom of both s26 and s27. The app's own code cites canvas 'screen 33' repeatedly (lines 32, 140, 258) -- STALE: current s33 is 'Portfolio' ('05 Portfolio and Wallet.dc.html'), not Asset detail.
screens.why: The watchlist-toggle and Buy/Sell-footer halves clearly map to s26/s27, but the app is missing the Order Book tab (a real, designed, distinct piece of the canvas's asset-detail experience) while adding ProductCard/dividend-stat content the canvas doesn't specify at all -- a human needs to decide whether Order Book ships and whether ProductCard content stays.

screens.purpose: Utility file, not a screen: `isNgxOpenNow()`/`marketNextOpenLabel()`/`marketClosedBannerSubtitle()` (WAT-timezone-correct NGX open/closed clock logic) plus the shared `KMarketClosedBanner` inline widget reused on Markets, Watchlist, and Asset Detail.
screens.evidence: Searched for 'Market closed' and 'opens 10:00am tomorrow'-style copy and found the canvas's closed-market treatment is a full, standalone, dedicated PUSH SCREEN (s39: back header, 'Market closed' status pill, hero last-traded price, a 'This price is not a promise' warning card, an 'If you order now' queue-explanation table, and Queue-a-buy/Set-a-price-alert footer buttons) -- not a small inline banner. The app's actual closed-market UI (`KMarketClosedBanner`) is a compact 2-line card (icon + 'The market is closed' + subtitle) embedded inline within other list screens, conceptually related to s39's title/subtitle copy but not the same artifact at all.
screens.why: This file is a shared utility/banner, not a page with its own route -- there is no artboard-shaped surface here to redesign against. Any redesign work belongs at the call sites (Markets, Watchlist, Asset Detail screens) that embed this banner, and separately, s39's much larger standalone 'Market closed' screen has no equivalent anywhere in the app at all (worth flagging to the human as its own gap, but not as a change to this helper file).

screens.evidence: Searched for 'Search companies' and 'Biggest gainers' -- both found on s24/s24d ('03 Home and Markets.dc.html', card-titled '24 · Markets'), which is the real current Markets screen. Shell matches: title, sector chip row (canvas: All/Banking/Telecoms/Consumer/Oil & gas; app: All + real distinct `Asset.sector` values), and a full-list AssetRow section headed 'All companies'. Gaps: s24 additionally specifies a 'Market mood today' feature card (green/red day sentiment, up/down counts, NGX All-Share index figure) and a 'Biggest gainers' horizontal-scroll rail, neither of which the app builds -- though the app's own comments (lines 22-28) already flag the NGX-index figure as a genuine, tracked backend gap (docs/redesign/BACKEND_GAPS.md) rather than a silent omission. Canvas also embeds a full SearchPill inline on the Markets page itself; the app uses a header search ICON button routing to a separate Search screen instead. The mechanical shortlist (s39 Market closed 0.355, s41 Orders hub 0.226, s40 Queued order 0.226) never surfaced s24 -- found by reading the full canvas file.
screens.why: Core purpose and list/filter structure map cleanly to s24; the missing Market-mood card and Biggest-gainers rail are additive content gaps (one already tracked as a backend blocker), not conflicting live features that would be destroyed by adopting the artboard.

screens.purpose: Pushed 'Price alerts' hub managing alerts across the investor's WHOLE watchlist at once: a featured card (first watchlist ticker) with ±3%/±5%/±10% percent-of-day-move preset chips plus a custom-₦-price field, and on/off toggle switches (default ±5%) for every other watchlist ticker; single 'Save alerts' footer button.
screens.evidence: Searched for 'preset' and '±' (percent-threshold syntax) across the whole canvas: the only hit is an unrelated 'Period presets or exact dates' phrase on the statements screen ('06 Account and Support.dc.html' line 360) -- no percent-of-move alert concept exists anywhere. The canvas's actual price-alert design (s49 'Set a price alert', s50 'My alerts') is a ONE-ALERT-PER-ASSET model: entered from a single asset's own page, an absolute ₦ price threshold with a Rises-above/Falls-below direction toggle (s49), landing in a flat list of individually-set alerts each showing distance-to-target with a per-row delete (s50) -- there is no 'manage every watchlist alert from one hub' screen, no percent-based presets, and no featured-ticker-vs-toggle-row split anywhere in the canvas.
screens.why: Both are 'price alerts' features in name, but the underlying data/UX model is fundamentally different (percent-move hub-style management vs. per-asset absolute-price alerts set from that asset's own page) and the app's version is backed by a real, already-shipped CRUD API (PriceAlertRepository) documented in this file's own header as deliberately reconciling the two. A human must decide whether to rebuild this screen against s49/s50's per-asset model (a real rewrite, not a restyle) or keep the hub model and just restyle it.

A human must decide whether to commission a new watchlist artboard, fold 'saved' state into the Markets/Asset-detail screens some other way, or restyle the existing screen in place.
